t.10.1: Aṣṭāvakra said: Abandoning desire, the enemy, and wealth, which is fraught with misfortune, and even dharma, the cause of these two, cultivate indifference toward everything.
t.10.2: Look upon friends, lands, wealth, houses, wives, inheritances and all such possessions as a dream or a magician's illusion, lasting only three or five days.
t.10.3: Wherever there is craving, know that there indeed is saṃsāra. Taking refuge in mature dispassion, be free of craving and be happy.
t.10.4: Bondage consists of craving alone, and its destruction is called liberation. It is merely through attachment to things that the satisfaction of attaining them arises, again and again.
t.10.5: You alone are pure consciousness; the world is inert and likewise unreal. Even ignorance is nothing at all, so what desire to know can you still have?
t.10.6: Kingdom, sons, wives, bodies and pleasures have perished for you in birth after birth, even though you were attached to them.
t.10.7: Enough of wealth, of desire, and even of virtuous deeds! Through these the mind has found no rest in the wilderness of saṃsāra.
t.10.8: Through how many births has painful and wearying action not been done with body, mind and speech? Let it cease, at least now.
